description: Build a shape-unified mixed-precision Cholesky around BF16x9 or TF32 tensor-core panels with selective FP32 residual repair: use resident batched kernels through n=1024 and recursive lower-only supernodes above it, repairing only unstable diagonal/frontier tiles while preserving exact fresh-input and caller-stream behavior.

Integrated the same-run shape-unified mixed-precision implementation from the baseline: resident custom n32/n64/n128 kernels, specialized n256 and batch60/n1024 owner paths, 64-wide FP32 frontier factors with TF32 lower-triangular updates for dense 4x1024/2x2048, BF16x9 cuSOLVER direct paths, and recursive lower-only mixed updates for n>=8192. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, six fresh-input cases, and all 15 benchmark cells passed. Aggregate measured 809.759 us; cells were 19.556/25.758/60.819/78.017 us at n32..256, 755.200 us at 4x1024, 1478.544 us at 2x2048, and 4912.442/14305.443/42282.327 us at n8192/16384/32768.

Extended the 64-wide FP32 frontier factor plus TF32 lower-triangular update route to dense batch16/n512, removing that direct cuSOLVER island while preserving exact handling for validation families. Wrapped build, all official/fresh validation, and all 15 cells passed. The changed n512 cell improved from 765.017 to 383.501 us in the queued comparison; aggregate improved from 809.759 to 780.134 us. Other target cells measured 753.521 us at 4x1024 and 1476.940 us at 2x2048.

Routed batch60/n1024 through the same 64-wide TF32 frontier path to test a fully unified resident-to-frontier dispatch. Wrapped build and all official/fresh validation passed, but the benchmark reached shape 7 and raised a grouped_factor_solve_ argument error because the shape-change allocator selected the mixed-path None info tensor for batch60 while the TF32 grouped factor requires an int32 info tensor. Logged before repair as required; earlier cells including batch16/n512 and 4x1024 ran correctly.

Repaired the unified batch60/n1024 TF32 frontier allocation by prioritizing the grouped factor's int32 info/workspace over the generic mixed-path allocation. Wrapped build, all official/fresh validation, and all 15 cells passed. The unified 64-wide frontier measured 1838.037 us at batch60/n1024 versus 963.533 us for the resident specialized path, while batch16/n512 remained 381.087 us and 4x1024/2x2048 were 751.798/1479.037 us; aggregate measured 812.225 us.

Restored the resident batch60/n1024 panel DAG while retaining the newly unified 64-wide TF32 frontier at batch16/n512 and the existing repaired low-batch n1024/n2048 routes. Wrapped build, full official/fresh validation, and all 15 cells passed. Aggregate measured a brief-best 778.130 us; batch16/n512 was 383.239 us, batch60/n1024 981.997 us, 4x1024 754.001 us, and 2x2048 1479.050 us.

Measured five trials from the plain cuSOLVER baseline. Integrated a same-run shape-unified mixed implementation with resident n32/n64/n128, specialized n256 and batch60/n1024, 64-wide FP32 frontier repair plus TF32 lower-only updates at low-batch n1024/n2048, BF16x9 direct paths, and recursive mixed lower-only large solves. Initial full-grid pass was 809.759 us under queued outliers. Extending the repaired TF32 frontier to batch16/n512 cut that cell from 765.017 to 383.501 us and measured 780.134 us aggregate. A fully unified batch60/n1024 attempt first exposed and logged an info-allocation runtime error; after repair it passed but measured 1838.037 us at that cell and 812.225 us aggregate, so the resident batch60 DAG was restored. Final clean HEAD 2012df9b81b263a34e6bbc3b7beaad0156bc587c passed wrapped build, all 17 official tests, all six fresh-input guard cases, and all 15 benchmark cells at a brief-best 778.130 us, with n512 batch16 383.239 us, n1024 batch4/batch60 754.001/981.997 us, n2048 batch2 1479.050 us, and n8192/n16384/n32768 4962.546/14331.155/42330.064 us. Final nsys capture was attempted twice through the required wrapper but the harness reported no generated capture-range report; the failed profile text is archived under the exact final SHA. Keep work going on selective runtime residual tests that choose exact repair only for unstable frontiers, a batch-aware grouped factor interface for batch60, BF16x9 correction products instead of the current TF32-only medium update, and recursive large supernodes narrower than 4096 with repaired diagonal tiles.

Continue the shape-unified mixed-precision design with a compiling MXF8/BF16 far-product prototype. Preserve FP32 diagonal/frontier repair, fuse quantization into panel publication, and begin with one lazy shape-scoped block-scaled operation using the installed SM100 template and alpha-beta C-load epilogue.
